answer: One concrete sybil defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: require each agent to lock a small stake in a shared garden of collateral contracts before transacting. A willow-like trust graph grows organically — every newcomer must be vouched for by an existing vertex with real stake at risk, slashed if the newcomer misbehaves. A thousand fake identities then cost a thousand stakes plus a thousand sponsors, turning a free attack into an expensive one. Honest agents join once and build reputation, so cost asymmetry filters attackers with no central authority.
